items.title: آنچه گذشت: نتانیاهو: تنها یک دولت وحدت ملی می‌تواند تهدید ایران را یک بار برای همیشه از بین ببرد
items.summary: بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست‌وزیر اسرائیل، بار دیگر خواستار تشکیل دولت وحدت ملی با گادی آیزنکوت، رقیب سیاسی خود شد و بر وعده‌اش برای از بین بردن تهدید ایران تاکید کرد. آقای نتانیاهو در پیامی ویدئویی گفت دیدار روز پنجشنبه ( ۱۲ نوامبر/۲۱ آبان) با گادی آیزنکوت، او را بیش از پیش به این باور رسانده است که تشکیل دولت وحدت ملی برای تضمین امنیت اسرائیل ضروری است. او افزود چنین دولتی می‌تواند «تهدید ایران را یک‌بار برای همیشه از بین ببرد.»

The new partnerships raise questions about whether Russia's efforts to attract foreign workers could help sustain drone production as its war against Ukraine continues. items.summary_original: Senate Republicans huddled for hours on end to define their remaining time in power and determine if the leadership they had backed so far was the right choice moving forward into a new era in Washington, D.C. Some closed-door meetings over the last nearly two years Republicans have controlled the Senate have been animated, with policy pitches devolving into shouting matches — President Donald Trump and Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., infamously sparred over the Iran war earlier this year. This confab, their first since Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and Democrats roared back into the majority, was different. In part, it was meant to develop a plan that would carry them through the final weeks of this year — that was agreed upon during the meeting, but not without its own drama after the fact on who could lay claim to the GOP’s 54-day blitz. SENATE GOP REBELLION FIZZLES AS THUNE KEEPS POWER DESPITE HISTORIC MIDTERM MASSACRE It was also a test to see if Republicans wanted to keep Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., as their leader, or delay until a challenger appeared. But Republicans pushing for a delay acknowledged part of the problem: Who would want the job? "I got the job because nobody else wants it," Thune told Fox News Digital after the dust settled in the Old Senate Chamber. items.summary_original: This article is Part 3 of a Fox News Digital exclusive series investigating trucking fraud, public safety, and assimilation concerns in southwest Ohio. You can read Part 1 here and Part 2 here . OHIO - An influx of Uzbek immigrants and trucking companies, coupled with mounting concerns about roadway safety and alleged fraud, is fueling frustration in southwest Ohio , where residents are speaking out about changes they say have left them feeling unsafe on their roads and increasingly uneasy in their own neighborhoods. Jane, a resident of southwest Ohio, is one of many who have been affected by the Uzbek influx, which she says ultimately drove her out of a new home she purchased in the area after just 18 months of living there. "I have literally been screaming about what has been going on for years, and I'm like somebody needs to take notice of this," Jane told Fox News Digital. Jane recounted repeated problems involving neighbors she identified as Uzbek, describing unsupervised children grabbing moving cars, climbing construction equipment, threatening to punch, kick or choke her dog, and taking her child's bicycle while ignoring demands to return it. She also described children urinating on neighbors’ vehicles, adults slaughtering chickens outdoors in view of her frightened child, and semi-truck cabs obstructing driveways. items.summary: نایب بوکله، رئیس جمهور السالوادور این هفته ویدئویی منتشر کرد که در آن نیروهای نظامی از سگ های روباتیک سوار بر تفنگ در عملیاتی برای بازپس گیری استادیوم هائیتی از کنترل باندها استفاده می کنند. بوکله در ترجمه ای از کریول هائیتی در X می نویسد: «بر اساس توافق دوجانبه بین دولت هائیتی و دولت السالوادور، یک عملیات مشترک شامل پلیس ملی هائیتی، نیروهای مسلح هائیتی (FAd'H)، نیروی ویژه و نیروهای ویژه سالوادور با موفقیت کنترل استادیوم سیلویو کاتور را به دست گرفت و آن را ایمن کرد. این ویدئو روبات‌ها را نشان می‌داد که در یک راهرو حرکت می‌کنند و از پله‌هایی با تفنگ بالا می‌روند. حمله هوایی با پشتیبانی السالوادور مقر باند هائیتی را در میان جست و جو برای سربازان مفقود نابود کرد، دقیقاً مشخص نیست که ربات ها چگونه به پورت کمک کردند
items.summary_original: El Salvador President Nayib Bukele released a video this week showing military forces using robotic dogs mounted with rifles in an operation to take back a stadium in Haiti from gang control. "Under the bilateral agreement between the Haitian government and the government of El Salvador , a joint operation involving the Haitian National Police, the Haitian Armed Forces (FAd’H), the Task Force, and the Salvadoran Special Forces successfully took control of Sylvio Cator Stadium and secured it," Bukele wrote on X in a translation from Haitian Creole. The video showed the robots moving down a hallway and up a set of stairs with the rifle on top. EL SALVADOR-BACKED AIR ASSAULT DESTROYS HAITI GANG HEADQUARTERS AMID SEARCH FOR MISSING TROOPS It’s unclear exactly how the robots assisted in the Port-au-Prince operation. Bukele said "several human skulls" were found inside the stadium during the operation. 'THEY FED HIM HIS OWN EARS': TOP REPUBLICAN SHARES HORRIFYING STORIES OF GANG RULE IN HAITI "We will now establish an operational base at the stadium so we can continue advancing deeper into territory controlled by the gangs," he said. "I'm not saying we're entering the dark age, but these are things that we have to preserve no matter what the atmosphere is in the country or the world at the time," Alito said during a fireside chat with Mollie Hemingway, editor-in-chief at the Federalist, which followed the Antonin Scalia Memorial Dinner at the 2026 National Lawyer's Convention in Washington D.C. The remarks come on the heels of the blue tsunami of the 2026 midterms, with Republicans losing 42 House seats and eight Senate seats, with the Alaska U.S. Senate race still uncalled. Democrats are set to take control of Congress with eight lawmakers backed by the Democratic Socialists of America. Both incoming and returning members have pressed for investigations and subpoenas targeting President Donald Trump and his administration. items.summary_original: Two American tourists drowned in the Bahamas after a strong current pulled a group of swimmers out to sea Friday, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said in a press release. The pair — a 38-year-old man and a 40-year-old woman — were swimming with a larger group in waters off the island of Bimini when the strong current swept them away. Police said the victims were swimming in an area beyond a sign warning of strong currents . MOM OF 2 WHO DIED RESCUING SONS DURING BAHAMAS SNORKELING TRIP IS IDENTIFIED A nearby ferry boat rescued some of the swimmers, but the American duo were already unresponsive by the time the boat got to them, police said. Though CPR was administered to the pair, they remained unresponsive. WOMAN FOUND FLOATING IN SEA AFTER GOING OVERBOARD FROM ROYAL CARIBBEAN SHIP "Both victims were transported to the local clinic, where medical personnel continued life-saving efforts. Unfortunately, despite their efforts, both individuals were pronounced deceased by the attending physician shortly before 4:00 p.m.," the police statement read. Police do not suspect foul play but are investigating the circumstances. ROBBERIES, ASSAULTS AND RAPES SPUR NEW US TRAVEL WARNING FOR POPULAR CARIBBEAN GETAWAY An autopsy will be conducted to determine the exact cause of death, according to the police. Fox News Digital contacted the Royal Bahamas Police Force for further information.

items.summary_original: Democrat senators are leaving the door open to eliminating the Senate filibuster as their party prepares to take control of the chamber. One lawmaker said the move must be on the table, while another warned it could be a "double-edged sword." "Obviously, the filibuster is something that has to be on the table," Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., told Fox News Digital when asked about Democrats' plans for the chamber. But Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., warned that changing the rules could carry consequences long after Democrats leave power. SCHUMER, JEFFRIES SIDESTEP QUESTIONS ON NUKING FILIBUSTER, LAUNCHING ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER BLUE WAVE "Some of these things that we see here can be very much a double-edged sword," Kim said. "I'm not saying that's to deter us from doing it if we decide to do it. But I wanna make sure that everyone's clear-eyed about what we're doing." Scrapping the Senate's 60-vote hurdle would allow Democrats to advance most legislation with a simple majority, weakening Republicans ' ability to block their agenda but also giving the GOP the same advantage if it regains control. Fox News Digital pressed the senators on whether Democrats would consider changing the rules while President Donald Trump remains in office or wait until a potential Democratic presidential victory in 2028. Paul Mitchell claimed in a San Francisco Chronicle op-ed published Wednesday that lawmakers should "kill partisan gerrymandering for good." He made the comments after California voters approved Proposition 50 in November 2025, temporarily replacing the state's independently drawn congressional districts with a Democratic-friendly map for elections through 2030. "I wasn’t trying to do this [op-ed] to time with anyone’s efforts to do further gerrymandering," Mitchell told Fox News Digital Thursday evening. "I always planned on doing this as soon as the election was over, and I even did a CNN interview with Elex Michaelson during the election coverage, where I said that the answer needs to be to stop this redistricting war and actually fix the problem. items.summary_original: Vice President JD Vance has long been viewed as President Donald Trump's heir apparent, but a string of developments following Republicans' bruising midterm losses is raising new questions about his potential path to the White House in 2028. Vance is facing criticism from some Republicans over his explanation for the party's election defeats, particularly his decision to blame the Iran war. Other prominent Republicans are beginning to draw support for potential 2028 bids, complicating the political picture for the vice president. The political debate follows a devastating election for Republicans, who lost their majorities in both chambers of Congress beginning next year, with at least 30 GOP House members losing their races. TRUMP SAYS HE DOESN’T DISAGREE WITH VANCE THAT IRAN WAR FUELED GOP LOSSES The losses have prompted competing explanations from within the party over what went wrong and what Republicans should do differently. Some of Vance's allies have reportedly urged him to consider sitting out the 2028 race after the midterm losses, The Wall Street Journal reported Nov. 7. However, others close to the vice president still expect him to run, The Washington Post reported Friday, underscoring the uncertainty surrounding his political future. A Vance ally pushed back on suggestions that the midterm losses have diminished his 2028 prospects, saying the vice president will decide whether to run on his own timeline. items.summary_original: FIRST ON FOX: President Donald Trump has made tariffs a centerpiece of his trade agenda, and businesses are spending more on D.C. bureaucrats to help navigate those rules. Rachel Greszler, who authored a new report from Advancing American Freedom (AAF), said companies are paying lobbyists to seek exemptions from tariffs instead of using that money to expand their businesses, hire workers or raise wages. A new report from former Vice President Mike Pence's group found that lobbying disclosures mention tariffs rising 239% in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the same period in 2024. The total spending reported on those filings jumped 337%, though it may include lobbying on issues beyond tariffs. A MUST-WIN MIDTERM STATE IS THE REAL LOSER OF TRUMP'S CANADA TRADE WAR "Affordability is top of mind for many Americans," Greszler told Fox News Digital, arguing that changing tariffs are raising costs, threatening jobs and squeezing paychecks. Businesses are responding by stepping up their lobbying efforts. Fourteen organizations spent more than $1 million on lobbying in the third quarter, up from two in the same quarter of 2024. Another 105 spent more than $100,000, compared with 26 two years earlier. Tariffs may also be affecting prices consumers pay. items.summary_original: ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — A senior Emirati official is warning that demonstrations in Europe have crossed a line from political expression into a national security threat, arguing that extremism must be confronted before it turns violent. "You can go demonstrate, talk, give a speech, but what [we] saw in the street in 11 cities in Europe is not freedom of speech. It is a threat to national security," Dr. Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, chairman of the Defense, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee of the UAE's Federal National Council, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview. The remarks come against a wider European debate over radicalization. On Nov. 3, Europol reported that authorities from 16 countries had referred more than 9,000 links to extremist and terrorist material appearing across 47 social media and gaming platforms. The operation targeted online role-playing content promoting jihadist, far-right, far-left and anarchist violence, including material that could draw minors toward extremist networks. I hope there is a bipartisan appetite on both sides to not only protect consumers but also target some of this fraud that is wasting so much of our tax dollars." items.summary: اختصاصی: جمهوری خواهان مجلس نمایندگان آماده نزاع به کنگره بعدی می روند. نماینده تام ایمر، نماینده حزب دموکرات، که سال آینده از شماره 3 قدرتمندترین جمهوری خواه مجلس نمایندگان به شماره 2 خواهد رسید، به فاکس نیوز دیجیتال گفت که جمهوری خواهان اکثریت جدید دموکرات ها را در دو سال آینده "مسئول" در قبال ایده های جناح چپ افراطی خواهد دانست، حتی اگر نتواند کنترل کند که چه طرح هایی رای می گیرند. ایمر، که در چهار سال گذشته به عنوان تازیانه اکثریت مجلس خدمت کرده است، روز سه شنبه به عنوان شلاق اقلیت در کنار جیم جردن، رهبر اقلیت مجلس نمایندگان در ایالت اوهایو انتخاب شد. رئیس مجلس نمایندگان به دموکرات‌ها واگذار می‌شود و احتمالاً حکیم جفریس، رهبر فعلی اقلیت، D-N.Y برنده خواهد شد. و علیرغم اینکه جفریس آماده است تا کنترل قوانینی را که به صحن مجلس می‌رسد در دست بگیرد، اِمر به جمهوری‌سازی مجلس هشدار داد.
items.summary_original: EXCLUSIVE: House Republicans are heading into the next Congress ready to brawl. Rep. Tom Emmer, R-Minn., who will rise from the No. 3 most powerful House Republican to No. 2 next year, told Fox News Digital the GOP will hold the new Democrat majority "accountable" for the far-left faction's ideas over the next two years, even if it cannot control what bills get a vote. Emmer, who has served as House majority whip the past four years, was elected Tuesday to serve as minority whip alongside incoming House Minority Leader Jim Jordan , R-Ohio. The speaker of the House position turns over to Democrats and will likely be won by current minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y. And despite Jeffries being poised to take control of what legislation gets to the House floor, Emmer signaled House Republicans would find ways to push their agenda as well. "We won," Trump said Wednesday. "It’s just a question of when we end it. I want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93% victory." John Alle, a business owner and co-founder of the Santa Monica Coalition, told Fox News Digital Raman won’t be able to "hide" the city’s homelessness problem from tourists arriving for the Games and raised concerns about potential gaps in her plan to deliver lasting results. "I don't think we're going to be able to hide that before the crowds," Alle said, adding that the city has become a "Third World country." 4 OF NATION'S LARGEST CITIES NOW LED BY SOCIALIST MAYORS AFTER TUESDAY'S ELECTION, AFFECTING TENS OF MILLIONS "We're not hiding it now. items.summary_original: Democrats are pushing major minimum-wage increases after their midterm victories, but economists warn the proposals could come with unintended consequences for small businesses and inexperienced workers. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro is pledging to more than double his state's $7.25 minimum wage, while Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker is calling for a federal increase as Democrats make affordability a central part of their governing agenda. The renewed push comes as Seattle, which has one of the nation's highest minimum wages, faces concerns about rising business costs and employment opportunities, raising questions about the tradeoffs of higher wage mandates. "We’re going to more than double Pennsylvania‘s minimum wage," Shapiro wrote in an X post this month. "Codify abortion rights into our state Constitution. Fund mass transit. Build more housing. These are the commonsense things that Pennsylvanians want done. AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI "And with a Democratic trifecta, we will deliver on all of them." Shapiro's proposal would raise Pennsylvania's minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour, an increase of roughly 107%, prompting questions about how small businesses would absorb the additional labor costs. items.summary_original: KENTON COUNTY, Ky. — Rep. Thomas Massie's push to impeach War Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war drew sharply different reactions from northern Kentucky residents interviewed by Fox News Digital. The residents offered competing assessments of the outgoing Republican congressman and whether his latest confrontation with the Trump administration reflects principle or political payback. Fox News Digital visited Covington, the population center of Massie’s district, along with Newport, Erlanger and other communities across the river from Cincinnati, to ask residents about their outgoing congressman and his efforts to impeach the Pentagon chief. TRUMP DEFENDS PENTAGON CHIEF AS MASSIE TARGETS HIM: 'HEGSETH SHOULD BE PRAISED, NOT IMPEACHED' Richard Hassebrock, a Covington resident who said he has not always agreed with Massie, welcomed the impeachment effort. "I'm not always a huge fan of Thomas Massie, but on this point I am," Hassebrock told Fox News Digital. Craig Cuskey, who works in the Covington area but lives just outside the bounds of Massie’s district in Louisville, described the impeachment push as "pure spite" and "petty," saying his opinion of the congressman had deteriorated. The contrasting reactions came after House Republicans voted to refer Massie's impeachment effort against Hegseth to committee, adding another confrontation to the Kentucky Republican's long-running disagreements with President Donald Trump and his party's leadership. items.summary_original: While Democrats’ midterm sweep dominated election night, voters in several states delivered consequential — and sometimes crosscutting — verdicts on voter ID, abortion access, taxes and English-language laws. But the down-ballot decisions largely unfolded beneath the shadow of the GOP’s crushing losses, offering a separate look at the policy priorities voters chose to elevate in their states. Read on to learn more about some of the most significant ballot measure results that will be shaping the lives of thousands of Americans. DEMOCRATS ‘DIVORCED FROM VOTERS’ AS 5 STATES BACK CITIZEN-ONLY VOTING, BOLSTERING GOP PUSH Voters in Nevada , North Carolina and Ohio all voted to pass voter ID requirements, even as talks among federal lawmakers have stalled on the issue, showcasing that the issue remains a point of public interest. In North Carolina, the state has required photo ID for in-person voting since 2018. But with the adoption of a constitutional amendment in a 59.6% to 40.3% vote, the Tar Heel State expanded the requirement to all forms of voting. Similarly, in Ohio, voters passed Issue 3 by a 65.3% to 34.6% vote. Although Ohio already had preexisting in-person voter ID laws, Issue 3 codified the requirement in the state’s constitution, making it harder to overturn later. Finally, in Nevada, Question 7 passed by a 62.1% to 37.8% vote, establishing a constitutional amendment to enact the state’s first voter ID requirement. items.summary_original: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has won Alaska's gubernatorial election, defeating Trump-endorsed Republican Bernadette Wilson and flipping the governor's mansion. The Associated Press called the race for Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state lawmaker, Friday evening. He is the first Democratic governor in Alaska since 1998. Alaska's gubernatorial election became an unusual contest as Republicans battled among themselves over who should succeed Gov. Mike Dunleavy, who was barred from seeking a third consecutive term. A BLUE WAVE IN GOVERNORS' MANSIONS COULD HURT FAMILIES MORE THAN A BLUE CONGRESS Wilson, a conservative activist and former political operative, received President Donald Trump's endorsement during a campaign in which multiple Republicans competed for the governor's office. Trump publicly criticized fellow Republicans Dave Bronson and Treg Taylor, accusing them of dividing conservative voters and potentially jeopardizing the party's hold on the governorship. Bronson, a former Anchorage mayor , and Taylor, a former Alaska attorney general, remained part of the Republican field, creating a complicated general election contest. ALASKAN POLITICAL SCION HOPES TO HOLD ONTO STATE'S SINGLE HOUSE SEAT Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state representative from Sitka , emerged as the Democratic contender, seeking to return his party to the governor's mansion after Dunleavy's two terms. items.summary_original: GOP firebrand Rep. Lauren Boebert , R-Colo., is projected to lose her seat in the House to Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher. The Associated Press made the call in the razor-thin race Friday afternoon in favor of Laubacher, who maintained her slim 48.7% lead over Boebert’s 47.9% once 99% of the ballots had been counted. GOP SENATOR SAYS REPUBLICANS CAN 'FORGET 2028' AS PARTY LOOKS TO RECLAIM UPPER CHAMBER Libertarian candidate Douglas Mangeris came in third with a little more than 3% of the vote. Laubacher is projected to win Colorado’s 4th Congressional District, according to the AP. Boebert was running for her fourth term in the state. She served her first two terms in Colorado’s third district and was running for her second term in the state’s fourth district. 2026 MIDTERMS: PRIMARIES, KEY RACES AND ELECTION RESULTS The 39-year-old congresswoman’s loss comes amid a blue wave that saw Democrats flip seats in Republican strongholds like Texas, Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi. Democrats now have 256 seats in the House of Representatives to Republicans’ 169. A party needs 218 for a majority. Several races nationwide remain uncalled nearly two weeks after Election Day. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

items.summary_original: The son of former CIA Director John Brennan was arrested for allegedly possessing child pornography, Fox News has learned. Kyle Brennan, 40, was charged with transportation of child pornography, according to a federal complaint. The case originated when Adobe CyberTipline reports flagged accounts linked to Brennan for uploading illicit files involving minors. In April and June 2024, Adobe submitted two reports to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) regarding an account allegedly used to upload suspected child sexual abuse material. FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS BLUE STATE'S LAW PROHIBITING ICE AGENTS FROM WEARING MASKS ON THE JOB The FBI's Washington field office is involved in the investigation . Around April 7, 2024, three files were uploaded to the Adobe account. A review of the files indicated a file that appeared to be a morphed image combining the face of a minor girl, later identified as a 12-year-old, with the naked body of another minor, federal prosecutors said. Comcast records showed that the IP address used to upload the files was registered to Kyle Brennan at an address in Warrenton, Virginia, where he lives. Records from Apple later confirmed that the private relay account was registered to Brennan, authorities said. items.summary: دنور - یک مایل بالاتر از بخش بزرگی از کشور، و چند لیگ دورتر از واشنگتن دی سی، رهبر اقلیت سنا، چاک شومر، دی-نیویورک، با شورشی پیشرونده ای مواجه است که تسلط او بر قدرت را تهدید می کند. این چالش توسط سناتور کریس ون هولن، دکتر، که از سال 2017 زیر نظر شومر خدمت کرده است، رهبری می‌شود. سال‌ها پیش، شومر تلاش کرد و نتوانست قوانین سنا را برای تصویب یک بسته حقوق رای به طور محدود تغییر دهد. جمهوری خواهان در دو سال گذشته با آن بازی کرده اند، اما هرگز ماشه را نکشیده اند. متحد سابق شومر در حالی که دموکرات ها با نبرد نادر قدرت داخلی مواجه می شوند، چالش رهبری را مطرح می کنند ون هولن گفت: «ما در سنای ایالات متحده به دموکراسی نیاز داریم و این به معنای اجازه دادن به یک مجلس بزرگ است.
items.summary_original: DENVER — A mile above much of the country, and leagues away from Washington, D.C., Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer , D-N.Y., is facing a progressive rebellion that threatens his grip on power. The challenge is being led by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who has served under Schumer since 2017. And he is willing to go further than Schumer ever has on one issue: terminating the filibuster. Years ago, Schumer tried and failed to narrowly change the Senate’s rule to pass a sweeping voting rights package. Republicans have toyed with it over the last two years, but never pulled the trigger. SCHUMER'S FORMER ALLY MOUNTS LEADERSHIP CHALLENGE AS DEMOCRATS FACE RARE INTERNAL POWER STRUGGLE Van Hollen said, "We need democracy in the United States Senate, and that means allowing, ultimately, a majority of senators to answer the call of the American people. "So, that means 51 votes. So, my personal view has been all along that the filibuster is an anti-democratic … provision. It's not in our Constitution," Van Hollen added. "It was put in there by senators to enhance their power over the power of the people." Van Hollen announced his challenge against Schumer , who has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade, Thursday night after a listening campaign with Senate Democrats. It presents a rare opportunity for Senate Democrats since there hasn’t been a contested Democratic leadership election since 1994. items.summary_original: Most of America bemoans political gridlock in the nation’s capital. DC area commuters deplore the city’s transit gridlock. But Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth may now be a fan of DC’s legendary traffic snarls. It appears that crosstown traffic may have prevented him from becoming only the third Cabinet secretary ever impeached by the House of Representatives. The House voted 211-204 this week to divert an effort by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) to impeach Hegseth. House Republicans moved to block a straight, up-or-down vote on impeachment. Instead, Republicans forced a vote on sending the articles to the Judiciary Committee. That’s where they’d go to die. If the House failed to sidetrack the articles, Members would have then voted on actual impeachment. If a simple majority voted to impeach, Hegseth would join 19th century Secretary of War William Belknap and former Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas as the only Cabinet Members impeached by the House. But DC’s streetside congestion altered the parliamentary traffic on the House floor. All Democrats said they were intent on impeaching Hegseth. But Republicans faced an attendance problem. Seven of their Members were missing. The vote on sending the impeachment articles to committee was tight. The tally read 204-204 at one point. By rule, tie votes fail. items.summary: دو مرد ایرانی روز پنجشنبه در بریتانیا به اتهام جاسوسی از روزنامه‌نگاران و منتقدان تهران محکوم شدند، آخرین موردی که زنگ خطر را در مورد عملیات ایران در خارج از خاورمیانه به صدا درآورد، زیرا فرانسه سپاه پاسداران انقلاب اسلامی را به حملات سایبری بی‌سابقه متهم می‌کند و یک مقام ارشد امارات نسبت به سلول‌های خواب ایرانی در خارج از کشور هشدار می‌دهد. این تحولات در حالی اتفاق می‌افتد که دولت ترامپ به کمپین فشار اقتصادی خود علیه تهران ادامه می‌دهد و درها را برای مذاکرات دیپلماتیک باز می‌گذارد و این پرسش‌ها را در مورد اینکه چگونه شبکه‌های اطلاعاتی خارج از کشور و فعالیت‌های مخفی ایران ممکن است در هر توافق آینده نقش داشته باشد، ایجاد می‌کند. هیئت منصفه دادگاه وولویچ تاج لندن، مصطفی سپهوند، 41 ساله و فرهاد جوادی منش، 46 ساله را به اتهام دست داشتن در رفتاری که احتمالاً برای کمک به یک سرویس اطلاعاتی خارجی پس از تلاش دادستان ها مجرم شناخته شدند.
items.summary_original: Two Iranian men were convicted in Britain on Thursday of spying on journalists and critics of Tehran, the latest case raising alarm over Iranian operations beyond the Middle East, as France accuses the IRGC of unprecedented cyberattacks and a senior UAE official warns of Iranian sleeper cells abroad. The developments come as the Trump administration continues its campaign of economic pressure against Tehran while leaving the door open to diplomatic negotiations, raising questions about how Iran's overseas intelligence networks and alleged covert activities might factor into any future agreement. A jury at Woolwich Crown Court in London found Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, guilty of engaging in conduct likely to assist a foreign intelligence service after prosecutors said they carried out surveillance of journalists and other individuals critical of the Iranian government, according to Reuters . According to prosecutors, the surveillance operation took place between August 2024 and March 2025 and involved visits to locations associated with the targets, photographs, videos and online research. items.summary_original: El Salvador's president on Tuesday said the country's military helped deliver a devastating air assault against the headquarters of one of Haiti's most powerful criminal gangs, which has been linked to mass kidnappings, weapons trafficking and extortion. Airstrikes targeted strongholds belonging to 400 Mawozo and the home of its leader, Lanmò San Jou, Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said. The attack took place Sunday near Port-au-Prince and was carried out by a Haitian police task force backed by Salvadoran troops, The Miami Herald reported . BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR The operation appears to be part of an ongoing military effort in response to the disappearance of four Salvadoran members of a U .N.-backed security mission abducted in a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince Oct. 18. "We kept our promise," Bukele said in a post on X. Videos showed several helicopters launching airstrikes against multiple compounds inside sprawling complexes. Dozens of people were also seen fleeing the properties on foot and motorbikes after the strikes. "Most of them ran away without even trying to fight. What cowards!" Bukele said. As many as 20 people are believed to have been killed in the operation, according to The Miami Herald, citing anonymous sources. items.summary_original: Iran claims it struck a small Omani island in the Strait of Hormuz , targeting oil tanker navigation infrastructure as CENTCOM maintains its blockade of Iranian ports and protects commercial shipping from Iranian attacks along the southern route. Three sources also confirmed to Reuters Wednesday that navigation systems and communications equipment on Didamar Island, also known as Little Quoin Island, had been attacked, raising concerns about the vulnerability of maritime infrastructure used to maintain oil shipments through the Gulf. Iran's semiofficial Fars News Agency reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy targeted the island, alleging the systems were being used to help vessels transit the strait without Tehran's authorization. WHITE HOUSE SILENT ON IRAN-OMAN HORMUZ PLAN TEHRAN SAYS WOULD BAN US WARSHIPS Iranian state television also claimed that personnel and equipment on the island "were helping the flow of oil smuggling by the enemy," with the IRGC maintaining it had carried out the strikes, Reuters reported. Video published by Reuters showed smoke rising near the rocky outcrop. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) said it identified the attack as occurring Nov. 8, before Iranian state media claimed responsibility on Nov. 10. ISW also questioned the extent of the reported damage, noting that commercial vessels continued using the southern route after the attack. items.summary_original: Unruly protesters set fires, smashed storefronts and launched fireworks at riot police across parts of Spain on Wednesday as a massive nationwide strike over soaring housing costs disrupted transportation and businesses. Violent scenes unfolded in Barcelona, where some demonstrators vandalized stores along the city's popular Paseo de Gracia shopping boulevard, set small bonfires and launched fireworks at officers arriving in riot gear and armored vehicles, according to The Associated Press . The violence erupted after a largely peaceful march as Spain experienced its first general strike in 14 years, with workers demanding relief from skyrocketing rents and the rising cost of living. TRAVELERS MAY FACE MAJOR DISRUPTIONS AS STRIKES THREATEN AIRPORTS AND POPULAR ATTRACTIONS Housing activists claimed 400,000 people marched through Barcelona, while city officials estimated attendance at 55,000. Government officials reported another 120,000 demonstrators gathered in Madrid despite heavy rain, the AP reported. The nationwide walkout disrupted public transportation, forced some businesses to close and blocked major roads. Police made arrests across the country, while officers used pepper spray against demonstrators in Madrid, according to the AP. items.summary: مقامات روز سه‌شنبه اعلام کردند که چهار خرس گریزلی از طریق شواهد DNA با حمله مرگبار به یک مادر و دختر در بریتیش کلمبیا مرتبط هستند که باعث شد افسران حیات‌وحش کانادایی هر چهار حیوان را بکشند. سرویس افسر حفاظت از بریتیش کلمبیا گفت که آزمایشات پزشکی قانونی به طور قطعی یک گریزلی ماده بالغ و سه فرزندش را با مرگ جنیفر بالکاراس، 48 ساله، و دخترش، سله رید، 20 ساله، در نزدیکی بلا کولا مرتبط دانست. بر اساس بیانیه 10 نوامبر آژانس، خرس ها در آخر هفته دستگیر و بر اساس دستورالعمل های استانی واکنش درگیری انسان و حیات وحش برای حفاظت از امنیت عمومی کشته شدند. جسد کوهنورد گمشده در خارج از مسیر کشف شد زیرا بازرسان به بررسی برخورد نادر مرگبار خرس می پردازند محققان تشخیص دادند که این برخورد احتمالاً شامل
items.summary_original: Four grizzly bears have been linked through DNA evidence to a deadly attack on a mother and daughter in British Columbia , prompting Canadian wildlife officers to kill all four animals, officials announced Tuesday. The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said forensic testing conclusively linked an adult female grizzly and her three offspring to the deaths of Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, near Bella Coola. The bears were captured over the weekend and killed in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety, according to a Nov. 10 statement from the agency. BODY OF MISSING HIKER DISCOVERED OFF TRAIL AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE RARE DEADLY BEAR ENCOUNTER Investigators determined that the encounter likely involved predatory behavior, although officials did not elaborate on how the attack unfolded. "This was a heartbreaking event for the families, the Nuxalk Nation and the Bella Coola community. We hope the efforts of everyone who responded, along with these findings, bring some measure of closure," said Insp. Jeff Tyre in a news briefing. More than a dozen conservation officers participated in the response, helping recover the victims, collect evidence and locate the bears while working in difficult terrain and weather conditions. "یک دیپلمات برجسته، یک رهبر باتجربه، همکار مهربان و مربی این زندگی را ترک کرده است. items.summary_original: Russia's Ambassador to the United States Alexander Darchiev, 66, died suddenly Wednesday, the Russian Foreign Ministry announced. "The leadership and staff of the Russian Foreign Ministry report with deep sorrow that on Nov. 11, at the age of 66, the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America, Alexander Nikitich Darchiev, passed away suddenly," Russia's statement , as translated to English, said. "A distinguished diplomat, experienced leader, kind colleague, and mentor has departed this life. A consummate professional and brilliant Americanist, A.N. Darchiev served on one of the most critical and demanding fronts of Russian foreign policy." "We express our deepest and most sincere condolences to the family and loved ones of Alexander Nikitich Darchiev," the statement added. "The cherished memory of our untimely departed colleague will forever remain in our hearts." items.summary_original: Israel's newly elected parliament was sworn in Tuesday, marking the beginning of a political transition that could end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's long tenure in power. Despite the opposition's parliamentary gains, the country remains without a new government, and negotiations to form one face significant obstacles. At the center of those negotiations is former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog on Sunday with assembling Israel's next governing coalition after 67 lawmakers recommended him for the position, compared with 46 who supported Netanyahu. Although Eisenkot's Yashar party won 21 seats in the Oct. 27 election , he is working closely with former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, whose B'Yachad party, formed with former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, secured another 12 seats. NETANYAHU FACES COALITION SHOWDOWN AS RIVALS MANEUVER TO FORM ISRAEL'S NEXT GOVERNMENT The two parties have not merged, but their cooperation effectively gives Eisenkot the negotiating backing of 33 lawmakers — more than Netanyahu's Likud, which remains the largest individual party in the Knesset with 27 seats. A source with knowledge of discussions within the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu told Fox News Digital that Bennett has decided to act as a political kingmaker, supporting Eisenkot's leadership bid rather than seeking the premiership himself. items.summary_original: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — In a historic house near Dubai Creek, a small gallery commemorating the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust stands alongside collections exploring Islamic civilization, Emirati heritage and the history of Palestine and the Holy Land. The Holocaust exhibition at the privately owned Crossroads of Civilizations Museum is among the first permanent displays of its kind in the Arab world. Opened in May 2021, less than a year after the UAE normalized relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords, it has become a symbol of the Emirates' approach to religious coexistence. During a recent visit to the museum, Fox News Digital saw displays documenting Nazi persecution, including a life-size image of the boy from the famous Warsaw Ghetto photograph, his hands raised in surrender. The gallery also tells the stories of Muslims who rescued Jews during the Holocaust, including Egyptian physician Mohammed Helmy, who sheltered Jews from Nazi persecution in Berlin. US-BACKED ISRAEL-MOROCCO DEAL DEEPENS ABRAHAM ACCORDS AMID GROWING REGIONAL THREATS But the story behind the exhibition is as personal as the objects it preserves. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, museum founder Ahmed Obaid Al Mansoori, a former member of the UAE's Federal National Council, explained that his passion for collecting historical artifacts began in childhood, when he inherited family manuscripts and objects from his grandparents. items.summary_original: The U.S. Air Force abruptly relocated more than a dozen aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England amid an emerging security threat, U.S. officials confirmed Tuesday. The Wall Street Journal first reported the move, citing sources who said the threat originated in Iran. As U.S. officials assessed the threat's nature and urgency, commanders raised the base's security level to Force Protection Condition Charlie, the military's second-highest alert level, indicating a likely terrorist threat against personnel or facilities. IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS Flight-tracking data and open-source analysts with the Military Air Tracking Alliance identified 13 U.S. aircraft leaving the base late Monday, the Associated Press said. Nine Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers were moved to airfields in Scotland, Germany and Spain. Three CV-22B Ospreys were relocated to nearby RAF Lakenheath, which has hardened aircraft shelters. A U.S. official told The Associated Press the moves were precautionary, noting that some aircraft were on rotational deployments while others were permanently stationed in the United Kingdom . IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY The move marks the second major relocation of U.S. military aircraft from Britain in less than two months. items.summary_original: A 7-year-old girl with dual U.S. and Mexican citizenship was shot and killed during a Mexican security operation targeting an alleged cartel member, and her mother accused police officers aboard a helicopter of firing the deadly shot. Aranza Aidelany Pardo died Oct. 29 in Matamoros, a Mexican border city across from Brownsville, Texas. She was among six people killed during the operation and subsequent roadblocks erected by the Gulf Cartel, according to The Associated Press. Her mother, Claudia Pardo García, told the AP that gunfire from a Tamaulipas state police helicopter struck her daughter in the head. Pardo was also wounded in the leg. Mexican authorities are investigating three officers aboard the helicopter who remain on active duty, according to Tamaulipas Public Security Secretary Carlos Arturo Pancardo. EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE TRUMP'S CARTEL CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE OFFICIAL DETAILS PRESIDENT'S PRIVATE BRIEFINGS The operation resulted in the arrest of Axel Alfredo Cárdenas Rodríguez, also known as El Titán, the son of an alleged Gulf Cartel leader and nephew of the group's imprisoned founder, Osiel Cárdenas Guillén. Pardo told the AP that she, her husband and their five children were returning home when they encountered cartel roadblocks and took a rural shortcut. She said a police helicopter began following their vehicle before circling in front of it. Her husband exited with his hands raised to show officers they were a family, but gunfire erupted. FBI برای مامور سابق اطلاعات نیروی هوایی متهم به جاسوسی برای ایران 200 هزار دلار جایزه می دهد.
items.summary_original: A senior U.S. Army soldier was arrested in England Tuesday on suspicion of espionage offenses related to Russia, according to U.K. police. The 41-year-old man, whose identity was not released, was detained as part of an investigation into suspected national security threats led by Counter Terrorism Policing , according to the Metropolitan Police. Officials said the arrest was carried out in coordination with the U.S. military and the FBI. "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. Herzog announced his decision on Nov. 7, but the formal presentation of the mandate is scheduled for Sunday, Nov. 8, at 5 p.m. Israeli time. Eisenkot will then have 28 days to assemble a government, with a possible 14-day extension. Netanyahu received the backing of 46 lawmakers, while seven members of the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party declined to endorse either candidate. Of the six dead, four are women and two are men, according to Małopolska Police. Shooting from a moving vehicle, the gunman allegedly targeted people at random, injuring civilians as well as police during the attack on Kraków's bustling Main Square. The perpetrator of the attack was shot and detained by police officers. Rescue services are still working at the scene," MPK S.A., the city's municipal public transport company, wrote in a statement shared to X. Video posted on social media showed people running while gunshots rang out. Police shot and wounded the suspect during a gunfight, and the area is now secured, according to authorities. The suspect, who has only been identified by police as a "citizen of the Republic of Poland," was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-style rifle to carry out the attack, Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Kraków police, told Polish network TVN24.
